sources.title: Effects of double-dose algebra on college persistence and degree attainment
sources.authors: Takako Nomi, Stephen W. Raudenbush, and Julia S. Smith
sources.finding: Chicago's double-dose algebra policy is a distinct extended-instruction case with evidence on high-school and postsecondary progression for students assigned around a prior-score cutoff.

sources.title: Principal Pipelines: A Feasible, Affordable, and Effective Way for Districts to Improve Schools
sources.finding: Across participating districts, pipeline schools with newly placed principals outperformed matched comparison schools after sustained implementation, alongside improved principal retention.
sources.caveat: The evaluation estimates a coherent district leadership package, not the isolated effect of one hiring, preparation, evaluation, or support component.

sources.title: Effects of Dual-Language Immersion Programs on Student Achievement: Evidence from Lottery Data
sources.finding: Lottery evidence reviewed by the What Works Clearinghouse supports potentially positive English-literacy effects for dual-language programs, with uncertain results in some other subjects.
sources.caveat: Program model, language pair, student composition, duration, and whether biliteracy is counted as an outcome all affect interpretation.

sources.title: Getting students on track for graduation: Impacts of the Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System after one year
sources.finding: In 73 randomly assigned high schools, EWIMS reduced chronic absence and course failure in year one but did not produce a detectable improvement in on-track credit accumulation.
sources.caveat: Implementation of the full process was difficult, and the first-year study does not establish an effect on graduation.

sources.title: The Causal Effects of Cultural Relevance: Evidence from an Ethnic Studies Curriculum
sources.authors: Thomas S. Dee and Emily K. Penner
sources.finding: A San Francisco pilot assigned around an eighth-grade GPA threshold produced large improvements in ninth-grade attendance, GPA, and credits earned for students near the cutoff.
sources.caveat: This is a high-fidelity, place-specific pilot; it should not be treated as evidence that every ethnic studies implementation will have the same effect.

sources.title: Impacts of Comprehensive Teacher Induction: Final Results from a Randomized Controlled Study
sources.finding: The national randomized evaluation found more support for treated beginning teachers but no consistent effect on retention, classroom practice, or student achievement for one-year induction.
sources.caveat: A later positive result for a two-year subset requires narrower interpretation and does not overturn the broadly null first- and second-year findings.

sources.title: Evaluation of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Program
sources.finding: A ten-site random-assignment evaluation found that participants were more likely to earn a diploma or GED, earn college credits, and work; earnings were higher after three years.
sources.caveat: The intensive residential alternative program serves a selected population of young people who are disconnected from conventional school pathways.

sources.title: The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Final Report: The Impact of Supplemental Literacy Courses for Struggling Ninth Graders
sources.authors: Marie-Andree Somers, William Corrin, Susan Sepanik, and colleagues
sources.finding: Across 34 high schools, supplemental literacy courses improved ninth-grade reading comprehension, core academic performance, and credit accumulation, but effects did not persist after the program year.
sources.caveat: The combined result masks differences between Reading Apprenticeship Academic Literacy and Xtreme Reading, and most students remained far below grade level.

sources.title: When Schools Stay Open Late: The National Evaluation of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Program
sources.finding: The federal after-school evaluation found few academic effects, improved perceived safety for elementary participants, and mixed developmental and behavior results.
sources.caveat: Attendance intensity was limited, and the study evaluates the program model and period studied rather than every modern after-school design.

sources.title: The Effect of Free School Meals on Household Food Purchases: Evidence from the Community Eligibility Provision
sources.authors: Michelle M. Marcus and Katherine G. Yewell
sources.finding: Universal free meals through Community Eligibility Provision exposure reduced household food purchases and was associated with improved dietary quality and lower food insecurity for lower-income households.
sources.caveat: This evidence concerns household and food-security outcomes; it does not by itself establish academic effects for students.

sources.title: Talent Development High Schools
sources.finding: The reviewed evidence did not show a discernible effect on progressing in school, despite a real large-high-school restructuring model aimed at attendance, achievement, and dropout prevention.
sources.caveat: The review covers a limited evidence base and should not be read as a verdict on every ninth-grade academy or small-learning-community implementation.

sources.title: The Impressive Effects of Tutoring on PreK-12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
sources.authors: Andre Nickow, Philip Oreopoulos, and Vincent Quan
sources.finding: Across experimental tutoring studies, tutoring produced meaningful average learning gains, with larger effects when programs were delivered during the school day, frequently, and by trained adults or near peers.
sources.caveat: The pooled estimate spans different grades, subjects, delivery models, and study settings; it does not establish that every tutoring implementation achieves the average effect.

sources.title: Examining the Effects of Schoolwide Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports on Student Outcomes
sources.authors: Catherine P. Bradshaw, Mary M. Mitchell, and Philip J. Leaf
sources.finding: In a five-year randomized trial across 37 elementary schools, trained schools implemented PBIS with high fidelity and had lower suspensions and office discipline referrals.
sources.caveat: The study's clearest impacts were behavioral and disciplinary; it should not be read as direct proof of broad academic gains in every PBIS implementation.

sources.title: Early College, Continued Success: Longer-Term Impact of Early College High Schools
sources.authors: Mengli Song, Kristina Zeiser, Drew Atchison, and Iliana Brodziak de los Reyes
sources.finding: Longer-term follow-up of early college admissions found sustained postsecondary benefits, including college enrollment and credential outcomes, for students offered access through oversubscribed schools.
sources.caveat: The design estimates effects for applicants to participating early colleges and does not automatically generalize to every dual-enrollment or early-college model.

sources.title: Head Start Impact Study: Final Report
sources.authors: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
sources.finding: The national randomized study found initial improvements in selected preschool outcomes, while many measured differences had narrowed by the end of kindergarten or first grade.
sources.caveat: Children assigned to the control group often used other early-childhood services, and the report's measured early-test convergence does not settle possible longer-run or non-test effects.

sources.title: The Impact of Restorative Practices on Student Outcomes in Pittsburgh Public Schools
sources.finding: A randomized evaluation of Pittsburgh's whole-school restorative-practices program found implementation and climate changes but did not find the expected broad reductions in suspension or improvement in academic outcomes during the study period.
sources.caveat: This evaluates a particular district rollout with uneven implementation; it does not establish that every restorative practice or narrower discipline intervention has the same effects.

sources.title: School Finance Reform and the Distribution of Student Achievement
sources.authors: Julien Lafortune, Jesse Rothstein, and Diane Whitmore Schanzenbach
sources.finding: Difference-in-differences evidence links post-1990 finance reforms to gains in district test scores, with larger gains for lower-income districts and narrower achievement gaps in many reform states.
sources.caveat: Effects vary with the reform's size and design, and a policy-induced association cannot identify the exact school-level uses of additional funding that produced the gains.

sources.title: Case Studies of Schools Receiving School Improvement Grants: Final Report
sources.authors: Kerstin Carlson Le Floch and colleagues
sources.finding: Case studies of 25 SIG schools document the implementation choices, capacity constraints, and sustainability challenges that accompanied the federal turnaround grants.
sources.caveat: The purposive case-study design supplies implementation context but does not estimate a causal effect on student outcomes.

sources.title: Evaluation of the Teacher Incentive Fund: Final Report on Implementation and Impacts of Pay-for-Performance Across Four Years
sources.finding: The randomized Teacher Incentive Fund evaluation found a positive fourth-year average achievement impact alongside substantial implementation and sustainability variation across grantees.
sources.caveat: The estimate is for a bundled federal pay-for-performance model, not for every merit-pay plan or for bonuses in isolation.

sources.title: An Evaluation of California Partnership Academies: Charting the Path from High School to Postsecondary Enrollment
sources.authors: Susan Sepanik, Kenny Nguyen, and Bryce Marshall
sources.finding: A newer randomized evaluation of the career-academy model found no overall effect on college readiness or first-year postsecondary enrollment at the point reported.
sources.caveat: The report covers early postsecondary outcomes; longer-term completion and labor-market reports are still pending.

sources.title: When Schools Stay Open Late: The National Evaluation of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Program New Findings
sources.authors: Mark Dynarski, Susanne James-Burdumy, Mary Moore, and colleagues
sources.finding: The federal evaluation's follow-on findings report separates outcomes for the randomized elementary sample and the matched middle-school sample, including safety and behavior measures.
sources.caveat: It is a companion analysis of the same national evaluation period, so it adds outcome detail rather than an independent program replication.

sources.title: Addressing Chronic Absenteeism in Schools: A Meta-Analysis of Evidence-Based Interventions
sources.authors: Katie Eklund, Matthew K. Burns, and Kari A. Oyen
sources.finding: The meta-analysis synthesizes school-based interventions intended to improve attendance and identifies variation by intervention type and study design.
sources.caveat: The reviewed interventions differ substantially in population, implementation, and attendance measure, so the synthesis is not a single program effect.

sources.title: Multiple Inference and Gender Differences in the Effects of Early Intervention: A Reevaluation of the Abecedarian, Perry Preschool, and Early Training Projects
sources.finding: A reanalysis of landmark randomized early-childhood programs assesses outcome families jointly and finds support for lasting benefits in several domains.
sources.caveat: The programs were unusually intensive, small, and historically specific; results do not establish effects for typical contemporary preschool.

sources.title: Effects of the Tennessee Prekindergarten Program on Children's Achievement and Behavior Through Third Grade
sources.authors: Mark W. Lipsey, Dale C. Farran, and Kelley Durkin
sources.finding: Follow-up of Tennessee's randomized pre-K evaluation reported that early advantages did not persist on the measured later achievement outcomes and documented concerning later behavioral patterns.
sources.caveat: The results concern Tennessee's program and comparison conditions during the study period, not every public pre-K model.

sources.title: Success Outcomes of Full-Day Kindergarten: More Positive Behavior and Increased Achievement in the Years After
sources.authors: John R. Cryan, Robert Sheehan, and Jane Wiechel
sources.finding: The study compares full-day and half-day kindergarten participation on later achievement and behavior outcomes.
sources.caveat: This is an older nonrandomized comparison, so selection and local program design limit causal interpretation.

sources.title: AI Literacy in K-12: A Systematic Literature Review
sources.authors: Lorena Casal Otero, Alejandro Catala, and Carmen Fernandez-Morante
sources.finding: The review maps K-12 AI-literacy research and implementation approaches, highlighting that the field is newer than the established tutoring evidence base.
sources.caveat: It reviews AI literacy rather than proving that generative-AI tutoring improves student learning outcomes.

sources.title: Effects of Dual-Language Immersion Programs on Student Achievement
sources.authors: Jennifer Steele, Robert Slater, and Gema Zamarro
sources.finding: Lottery-based evidence estimates the effects of access to dual-language immersion programs on student achievement.
sources.caveat: Results depend on the language model, school context, applicant group, and time spent in the program.

sources.title: The Impact of Induction and Mentoring Programs for Beginning Teachers: A Critical Review of the Research
sources.authors: Richard M. Ingersoll and Michael Strong
sources.finding: The review finds that induction and mentoring evidence is generally favorable for teacher commitment and practice, while effects vary by program design and outcome.
sources.caveat: It synthesizes heterogeneous programs and includes studies with different comparison designs, so it is not an estimate for one comprehensive induction model.

sources.title: Free Lunch for All! The Effect of the Community Eligibility Provision on Academic Outcomes
sources.authors: John Gordanier, Orgul D. Ozturk, and Breyon Williams
sources.finding: The study estimates academic-outcome changes associated with schools adopting the Community Eligibility Provision.
sources.caveat: Adoption is not random, and results depend on the policy setting, eligible schools, and outcome measure.

sources.title: Reengaging High School Dropouts: Early Results of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Program Evaluation
sources.authors: Dan Bloom, Alissa Gardenhire-Crooks, and Conrad Mandsager
sources.finding: Early randomized evaluation results document reengagement outcomes for participants in the residential National Guard Youth ChalleNGe program.
sources.caveat: The early follow-up does not answer the same longer-run employment and earnings questions as later reports.

sources.title: Core Knowledge Language Arts
sources.finding: The What Works Clearinghouse intervention report reviews eligible research on Core Knowledge Language Arts and its literacy outcomes.
sources.caveat: A clearinghouse review is limited to the studies meeting its screening rules and should not be read as an effect for every knowledge-rich curriculum.

sources.title: The Effect of Teacher Coaching on Instruction and Achievement: A Meta-Analysis of the Causal Evidence
sources.authors: Matthew A. Kraft, David Blazar, and Dylan Hogan
sources.finding: The meta-analysis pools causal evaluations of teacher coaching and reports larger effects on instructional practice than on student achievement.
sources.caveat: Average results mask variation in coaching dose, subject focus, coach expertise, and scale.

sources.title: Does Teacher Preparation Matter? Evidence about Teacher Certification, Teach for America, and Teacher Effectiveness
sources.authors: Linda Darling-Hammond, Deborah Holtzman, and Su Jin Gatlin
sources.finding: The analysis compares teacher preparation pathways and reported student-achievement differences in the California context.
sources.caveat: This is not a randomized comparison and has been debated; it is included as a contrasting pathway study, not a decisive estimate.

sources.title: Continued Progress: Promising Evidence on Personalized Learning
sources.authors: John F. Pane, Elizabeth D. Steiner, Matthew Baird, and Laura S. Hamilton
sources.finding: RAND's follow-up report compares participating personalized-learning schools with matched comparison schools and describes implementation conditions alongside achievement findings.
sources.caveat: The participating schools were early adopters and the study does not isolate one product, platform, or practice as the cause of observed differences.

sources.title: College Preparatory Curriculum for All: Academic Consequences of Requiring Algebra and English I for Ninth Graders in Chicago
sources.authors: Elaine Allensworth, Takako Nomi, Nicholas Montgomery, and Valerie E. Lee
sources.finding: The peer-reviewed analysis examines Chicago's ninth-grade college-preparatory requirement, including course performance and academic consequences.
sources.caveat: The district policy changed several elements at once and does not establish the effect of Algebra I alone in every setting.

sources.title: The Postsecondary Achievement of Participants in Dual Enrollment: An Analysis of Student Outcomes in Two States
sources.authors: Melinda Mechur Karp, Juan Carlos Calcagno, and Katherine L. Hughes
sources.finding: The study compares postsecondary outcomes for dual-enrollment participants and similar nonparticipants in two states.
sources.caveat: Participation is not randomly assigned, and the estimate is sensitive to the comparison construction and state policy context.

sources.title: The Impressive Effects of Tutoring on PreK-12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
sources.authors: Andre Nickow, Philip Oreopoulos, and Vincent Quan
sources.finding: The experimental tutoring synthesis provides comparative evidence relevant to both in-person and technology-supported high-dosage tutoring models.
sources.caveat: The review does not isolate the effects of one branded tutoring provider or software platform.

sources.title: The Impact of Enhancing Students' Social and Emotional Learning: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Universal Interventions
sources.finding: The meta-analysis synthesizes universal school-based SEL interventions across social-emotional, behavioral, and academic outcomes.
sources.caveat: Interventions vary in curriculum, delivery quality, and measurement, so average effects do not identify one required SEL model.

sources.title: A Review of Research on Project-Based Learning
sources.finding: The review assesses the then-available research on project-based learning, including achievement and implementation questions.
sources.caveat: The underlying studies are heterogeneous and many predate current standards, assessments, and digital tools.

sources.title: The Causal Effects of Cultural Relevance: Evidence from an Ethnic Studies Curriculum
sources.authors: Thomas S. Dee and Emily K. Penner
sources.finding: The published analysis estimates effects of San Francisco's ethnic-studies assignment rule for students near the eligibility cutoff.
sources.caveat: The design is most informative at the cutoff and for the district's particular curriculum and implementation.

sources.title: The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Study: Early Impact and Implementation Findings
sources.authors: James J. Kemple, William Corrin, Elizabeth Nelson, and colleagues
sources.finding: The early report describes implementation and first-year impacts for the randomized supplemental literacy-course evaluation.
sources.caveat: It is an earlier follow-up from the same research program and does not answer longer-term persistence questions.

sources.title: Making Progress Toward Graduation: Evidence from the Talent Development High School Model
sources.authors: James J. Kemple, Corinne Herlihy, and Thomas E. Smith
sources.finding: The evaluation compares outcomes in Talent Development high schools and comparison schools during implementation of the restructuring model.
sources.caveat: The comparison design and bundled school changes make it difficult to isolate individual model components.

sources.title: National Early Literacy Panel: Developing Early Literacy
sources.finding: The panel synthesizes evidence on early literacy skills and instructional practices that predict later conventional literacy.
sources.caveat: It is a synthesis of early-literacy research, not a new evaluation of the National Reading Panel itself.

sources.title: Community Schools as an Effective School Improvement Strategy: A Review of the Evidence
sources.finding: The evidence review synthesizes evaluations of integrated student supports and community-school strategies.
sources.caveat: Community schools are multi-component models, and the review does not identify a single universally effective service bundle.

sources.title: The Effects of Teacher Evaluation on Teacher Performance
sources.authors: Thomas S. Dee and James Wyckoff
sources.finding: The study evaluates changes in teacher performance associated with a high-stakes teacher evaluation system in Washington, DC.
sources.caveat: It estimates effects in one district's system and cannot separate every component of feedback, observation, dismissal, and incentives.

sources.title: Project Follow Through
sources.finding: The program archive documents the history, models, and published results associated with the federal Project Follow Through initiative.
sources.caveat: This is a program-hosted historical resource and should be read alongside independent analyses of the original evaluation.

sources.title: The Harlem Children's Zone: Promise Neighborhoods and the Neighborhood Effects Debate
sources.authors: Roland G. Fryer Jr. and Will Dobbie
sources.finding: The study analyzes student achievement in Harlem Children's Zone schools and considers the role of the school model and neighborhood services.
sources.caveat: The design cannot cleanly separate school effects from selection, location, and the surrounding support network.

sources.title: Student Achievement in Public Magnet, Public Comprehensive, and Private City High Schools
sources.finding: The study compares achievement patterns across magnet, comprehensive public, and private urban high schools.
sources.caveat: School enrollment is selective, so observed differences do not establish the causal effect of magnet-school attendance.

sources.title: Principal Pipelines: A Feasible, Affordable, and Effective Way for Districts to Improve Schools
sources.finding: The report evaluates district principal-pipeline systems using matched comparison schools and implementation evidence.
sources.caveat: The package combines multiple leadership investments and cannot isolate one hiring, preparation, or support component.

sources.title: Learning from Summer: Effects of Voluntary Summer Learning Programs on Low-Income Urban Youth
sources.finding: The randomized study reports effects of voluntary district summer-learning programs and relates outcomes to attendance and instructional conditions.
sources.caveat: Effects depend on participation and local program quality; a voluntary summer offer is not equivalent to mandatory extended schooling.

initiatives.name: A Nation at Risk / modern standards movement
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Raise expectations by making academic standards, assessment, and public accountability central to schooling.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: State standards, graduation requirements, public reporting, assessment emphasis
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Historical synthesis; state trend evidence
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP, state tests, graduation requirements
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Hard to isolate from demographic, fiscal, and accountability changes that followed.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Important agenda-setting reform, but not a discrete intervention with clean causal estimates.

initiatives.name: Goals 2000 / standards-based reform
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Encourage states to define rigorous goals and align curricula and assessments.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Standards adoption, planning grants, assessment alignment
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Historical/descriptive; state panel comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: State assessments, NAEP, graduation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: State standards differed widely; implementation and assessment quality varied.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Helped institutionalize standards-based reform but evidence is mostly indirect.

initiatives.name: State test-based accountability before NCLB
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use public test results and consequences to focus schools on achievement.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Test frequency, rating systems, sanctions/rewards, proficiency thresholds
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: State panel, NAEP trend, difference-in-differences
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP math/reading, state proficiency, gaps
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Researchers use NAEP to avoid state test inflation, but cross-state accountability intensity is hard to code.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Pre-NCLB accountability often raised measured math achievement more than reading, with risks of narrowing and gaming.

initiatives.name: No Child Left Behind
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Annual testing, subgroup reporting, and sanctions should pressure schools to improve proficiency for all groups.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Annual grades 3-8 testing, AYP targets, sanctions, public reporting, subgroup accountability
initiatives.targetPopulation: All public schools receiving federal funds
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: NAEP state panel; event study; state accountability comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP scale scores, state proficiency, subgroup gaps
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Best comparisons use NAEP rather than state tests because state cut scores and test stakes changed.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Evidence points to some math gains, weaker reading effects, and substantial incentives to narrow curriculum or game thresholds.

initiatives.name: Race to the Top
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Competitive funding would induce states to adopt coherent reforms in standards, data, teacher evaluation, and turnaround.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Grant dollars, Common Core incentives, data systems, teacher evaluation, turnaround plans
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: State comparisons; policy implementation surveys; achievement trend analysis
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP, state tests, policy adoption, teacher evaluation implementation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Winners differed from non-winners before grants; reforms were bundled and adoption was political.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Large policy adoption effects; achievement effects were not consistently strong or easy to attribute.

initiatives.name: School Improvement Grants
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Concentrated funds and prescribed turnaround models should change the lowest-performing schools quickly.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Turnaround, transformation, restart, closure models; leadership changes; staffing; extended time
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Regression discontinuity; implementation study
initiatives.outputsMeasured: State test scores, graduation, school practices
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Cutoff-based RD compares schools near eligibility thresholds, not all low-performing schools.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The national evaluation found weak average impacts despite large funding; implementation and model quality varied.

initiatives.name: ESSA evidence tiers and evidence-based intervention requirements
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Classify and encourage use of interventions backed by rigorous evidence.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Evidence tier rules, grant requirements, intervention review standards
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Evidence standards framework
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Evidence tiers, study quality, implementation plans
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Tiers are about evidence strength, not guaranteed local effect; external validity still matters.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Useful infrastructure for comparing studies, but it does not itself improve learning without good implementation.

initiatives.name: Common Core State Standards and aligned assessments
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Common, higher standards and aligned tests should make expectations clearer and improve college readiness.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: ELA/math standards, test alignment, teacher guidance, curriculum shifts
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Implementation studies; teacher panels; state trend analysis; C-SAIL design
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP, state tests, teacher knowledge/practice, assessment alignment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Adoption timing overlaps with recession, NCLB waivers, RTT, assessment changes, and local curriculum decisions.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Implementation was uneven; evidence does not support the idea that standards alone generate large achievement gains.

initiatives.name: Mississippi Literacy-Based Promotion Act / 'Mississippi miracle'
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Pair early screening, teacher training, coaching, interventions, and third-grade promotion rules to improve early reading.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: K-3 literacy instruction, phonics emphasis, reading coaches, intervention plans, retention/promotion threshold
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: State trends; NAEP comparison; RD/quasi evidence on retention
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Third-grade reading pass rates, NAEP grade 4 reading, state ELA, retention and exemptions
initiatives.normalizationIssues: NAEP gains are state-level and bundled; retention changes who appears in grade 4, so researchers analyze both policy components and cohort composition.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Mississippi is one of the most cited recent literacy success cases, but the causal mechanism is a policy bundle rather than one isolated program.

initiatives.name: Science of Reading state policy wave
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Move teacher preparation and classroom practice toward explicit, systematic instruction in foundational reading skills plus language comprehension.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Teacher prep standards, licensure tests, curriculum bans/approvals, coaching, screeners
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Implementation studies; state trend comparisons; emerging causal work
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Screeners, state reading scores, NAEP, curriculum adoption, teacher knowledge
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Policies differ in what they mandate; teacher knowledge and classroom fidelity are not the same as law passage.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Highly influential and evidence-aligned in direction, but cross-state causal estimates are still emerging.

initiatives.name: National Reading Panel synthesis
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Identify components of reading instruction with experimental or quasi-experimental support.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Evidence review of phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Systematic evidence review
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Effect sizes by reading domain
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The review synthesized studies rather than evaluating a single program; later policies sometimes oversimplified the findings.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: It became the foundation for much of the phonics/science-of-reading policy debate.

initiatives.name: Reading First
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Fund scientifically based reading instruction and assessment systems in high-poverty schools.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Reading coaches, PD, K-3 curricula, assessment, instructional time
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Regression discontinuity; randomized component; implementation study
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading comprehension, decoding, instruction time, teacher practice
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The evaluation tests the federal grant implementation, not the National Reading Panel findings themselves.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Improved some reading instruction measures but did not produce clear broad comprehension gains in the national impact study.

initiatives.name: Success for All
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use a coherent literacy block, frequent assessment, grouping, tutoring, family support, and schoolwide facilitation.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: 90-minute reading block, cooperative learning, assessments, tutoring, facilitator, family supports
initiatives.targetPopulation: Pre-K to grade 8, especially high-poverty schools
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; WWC intervention reviews; meta-analysis
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading achievement, phonics, comprehension, school implementation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Effects depend on fidelity and whole-school adoption; comparisons should account for program maturity.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: One of the better-studied comprehensive literacy models, with positive evidence in multiple reviews.

initiatives.name: Reading Recovery
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Provide intensive one-to-one tutoring to struggling first-grade readers before failure compounds.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Daily 1:1 lessons, trained teachers, early identification, discontinuation rules
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; WWC review; longitudinal follow-up debates
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Literacy achievement, writing, decoding, reading levels
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Selection, attrition, cost, and fadeout are central; ITT and treatment-on-treated estimates can diverge.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Short-run reading gains are supported in some studies, but cost, scale, and longer-run durability remain contested.

initiatives.name: Balanced literacy / workshop models
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Build authentic reading/writing habits through leveled texts, mini-lessons, choice, and teacher conferences.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Leveled readers, independent reading, cueing, writing workshop, classroom libraries
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Implementation studies; curriculum comparisons; descriptive district trend evidence
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading comprehension, decoding, motivation, state reading scores
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The label covers diverse practice; some classrooms included phonics while others underemphasized decoding.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Popular and influential, but evidence concerns about weak systematic decoding instruction drove many recent curriculum changes.

initiatives.name: Direct Instruction / Project Follow Through
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use explicit, scripted, sequenced instruction with high practice and immediate feedback.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Scripted lessons, mastery tests, teacher pacing, explicit modeling, corrective feedback
initiatives.targetPopulation: Elementary students, historically including high-poverty sites
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Long-term follow-up; quasi-experimental and program evaluations
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Standardized tests, dropout, college application
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Follow Through comparisons are historically important but not designed like modern multisite RCTs.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A major counterexample to claims that highly explicit instruction is inherently low-level.

initiatives.name: Core Knowledge / knowledge-rich curriculum
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Reading comprehension and civic learning improve when students build systematic background knowledge across domains.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Sequenced content, literature/history/science knowledge, vocabulary, curriculum coherence
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lottery/RCT in charter setting; quasi and implementation studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading, math, science, state tests, vocabulary
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Effects may reflect school model plus curriculum; generalizing outside participating schools requires care.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Recent causal work finds promising long-term reading gains, supporting a content-rich view of comprehension.

initiatives.name: High-quality instructional materials initiatives
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Better materials plus aligned professional learning can improve daily instruction at scale.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Curriculum adoption, EdReports-style signals, PL, district mandates/recommendations
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Teacher surveys; adoption studies; quasi evaluations
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Material adoption, standards alignment, teacher use, achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Adoption is not usage; researchers measure fidelity, teacher adaptation, and alignment to avoid treating procurement as implementation.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Materials matter, but effects depend heavily on supports and classroom use.

initiatives.name: High-dosage tutoring
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Frequent individualized or small-group tutoring accelerates learning by adding feedback-rich instructional time.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Tutor-student ratio, session frequency, total hours, during-school scheduling, curriculum alignment
initiatives.targetPopulation: Students below grade level; pandemic recovery; all grades with emphasis on math/reading
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; meta-analyses; implementation studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Math and reading test scores, course passing, attendance
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Normalize by cumulative hours, frequency, tutor type, group size, and whether tutoring occurs during the school day.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: One of the strongest short-run academic interventions when frequent, sustained, curriculum-aligned, and attended.

initiatives.name: Saga-style and tech-infused tutoring
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Combine high-dosage human tutoring with software, diagnostics, and structured curricula to improve math.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Daily/scheduled tutoring, tutor training, diagnostic software, small groups
initiatives.targetPopulation: Middle and high school math students
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; district pilots; cost studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Math test scores, course grades, credits
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Distinguish the tutoring relationship from software contribution; compare intended vs attended sessions.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Strong evidence for intensive tutoring models; the technology role is a support, not the whole treatment.

initiatives.name: Project STAR / class-size reduction
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Smaller K-3 classes increase teacher attention and student engagement, improving early learning and later outcomes.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Class size, teacher-student ratio, aide condition
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Randomized experiment; long-term administrative linkage
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Early test scores, college attendance, earnings, savings, home ownership
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Random assignment within schools is unusually strong; scaling requires enough effective teachers and classrooms.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Small early classes produced lasting benefits, but broad policy is expensive and sensitive to teacher labor supply.

initiatives.name: Teacher coaching
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Sustained, individualized coaching changes instruction more reliably than one-off workshops.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Coach visits, observation-feedback cycles, modeling, practice, video review, curriculum-aligned support
initiatives.targetPopulation: Teachers, especially early literacy and math
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Meta-analysis of causal studies; RCTs
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Instructional practice ratings, student achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Normalize by coaching cycles, coach expertise, content focus, and program scale; scaling effects are often smaller.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Coaching has stronger evidence than generic PD, especially at smaller scale and with clear instructional focus.

initiatives.name: Traditional workshop professional development
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Improve practice through training sessions, materials, and awareness of new standards or programs.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: PD hours, workshops, summer institutes, training materials
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs/quasi; reviews; implementation studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Teacher knowledge, practice, student scores
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Seat hours are a weak measure; compare content specificity, active practice, coaching, and curriculum alignment.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Often weak when isolated from coaching, materials, and accountability for classroom use.

initiatives.name: Teach For America and alternate-route pipelines
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Recruit academically strong candidates into hard-to-staff schools and support them with alternative preparation.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Selection criteria, summer training, school placement, support, service commitment
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs/quasi evaluations; teacher value-added comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Student math/reading gains, teacher retention, placement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Teacher assignment is not random in most settings; subject, grade, and retention matter.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Some evaluations show positive math effects, but reading effects and turnover tradeoffs vary by context.

initiatives.name: National Board Certification and advanced credentials
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Credentialing should identify and reward accomplished teachers, improving teacher quality and distribution.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Certification standards, incentives, teacher career ladders
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Observational/value-added; selection-adjusted comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Teacher retention, value-added, student scores
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Certified teachers are selected; researchers need prior performance and assignment controls.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Credentials can signal quality, but the policy question is whether incentives change who teaches where.

initiatives.name: Teacher merit pay / POINT and similar incentives
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Performance bonuses will motivate teachers to raise student achievement.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Bonus size, eligibility, test-score formula, individual/team incentives
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Randomized trials; quasi evaluations
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Student test scores, teacher behavior, retention
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Need account for baseline incentives, test stakes, collaboration vs competition, and whether teachers know how to improve.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Simple test-score bonuses alone have often produced null or modest effects.

initiatives.name: DC IMPACT / teacher evaluation with consequences
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Combine multiple teacher performance measures with incentives and dismissal risk to improve workforce quality.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Observation rubrics, value-added, ratings, bonuses, dismissals, professional development
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Difference-in-differences; regression discontinuity around rating thresholds; administrative data
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Teacher performance, retention, student achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Compare teachers near rating cutoffs; distinguish incentive, selection, and support mechanisms.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: More consequential evaluation can change teacher performance and composition, but sustainability and trust are central concerns.

initiatives.name: Gates Measures of Effective Teaching Project
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use multiple measures to understand and predict effective teaching.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Classroom observations, student surveys, value-added, video analysis
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Research study with random assignment of classrooms in validation year
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Measure reliability, predictive validity, student achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The project studied measurement validity; using measures in high-stakes systems is a separate policy intervention.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Influential for teacher evaluation design, but not itself a school improvement program.

initiatives.name: Gates Intensive Partnerships for Effective Teaching
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Better teacher effectiveness measures and talent systems should increase access to effective teaching.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Evaluation systems, staffing, compensation, tenure, PD, value-added, observations
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Longitudinal implementation and impact evaluation
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement growth, teacher effectiveness distribution, HR outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Bundled reforms, local implementation, and changing district contexts complicate attribution.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The initiative did not deliver broad expected student achievement gains despite major investment and implementation effort.

initiatives.name: Gates-funded small high schools / NYC Small Schools of Choice
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Smaller, mission-focused schools improve personalization, engagement, and graduation outcomes.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: School size, admissions choice, thematic focus, personalization, new school creation, closure of large schools
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lottery-based evaluation using high school choice system
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Graduation, credits, Regents exams, college enrollment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Lottery estimates apply to applicants to oversubscribed small schools; school closure and system redesign are part of context.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: NYC small schools produced meaningful graduation gains, showing school design can matter when implementation and choice systems align.

initiatives.name: Gates personalized learning / Next Generation Learning Challenges
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Customize pace, path, place, and learner goals using data, flexible grouping, and technology.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Adaptive software, competency progression, student choice, flexible schedules, data dashboards
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Matched comparison; implementation study; site visits
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Math and reading growth, student surveys, implementation measures
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The treatment is a heterogeneous school model, not just software; compare active usage and teacher mediation.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Early RAND evidence was promising, but heterogeneity and later critiques caution against treating personalized learning as one proven model.

initiatives.name: Gates Networks for School Improvement
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Networked continuous improvement helps schools identify problems, test changes, and spread effective practices.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Intermediary support, CI cycles, shared aims, data use, student voice, cross-school learning
initiatives.targetPopulation: Middle/high school transitions and postsecondary readiness
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCT and quasi evaluation; implementation study
initiatives.outputsMeasured: 9th-grade on-track, course failures, attendance, FAFSA, postsecondary enrollment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Impacts vary by network; researchers compare schools with stronger engagement and use targeted outcomes rather than broad test scores only.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The final evaluation found promising effects on some targeted outcomes, with engagement and CI fidelity tied to stronger results.

initiatives.name: Charter schools overall
initiatives.theoryOfAction: School autonomy plus family choice can create better school models and accountability through enrollment.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Autonomy, authorizer rules, school model, staffing, discipline, curriculum, CMO support
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lottery studies; virtual matched controls; state panels
initiatives.outputsMeasured: State tests, NAEP-like growth, graduation, college enrollment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Average charter effects hide major variation by state, authorizer, urbanicity, and school model; lottery samples are applicant populations.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Charter effects are highly heterogeneous: urban/no-excuses and some CMOs show strong gains, while many charters are neutral or weaker.

initiatives.name: No-excuses charter networks and high-performing CMOs
initiatives.theoryOfAction: High expectations, longer time, intensive tutoring, data use, and tight culture raise achievement in underserved communities.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Longer day/year, tutoring, behavior systems, teacher coaching, curriculum, data meetings
initiatives.targetPopulation: Urban charter students, often lottery applicants
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Admissions lotteries; matched comparison; CMO evaluations
initiatives.outputsMeasured: State tests, AP/SAT, college enrollment, behavior
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Lottery applicants may not represent all students; attrition and peer/compliance mechanisms need scrutiny.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Some networks generate large test-score gains, but the debate is about replication, student experience, and which mechanisms matter.

initiatives.name: Private school vouchers / DC and Louisiana examples
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Giving families public funds for private schools increases match quality and competitive pressure.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Scholarship amount, eligibility, private school participation, admissions lotteries, accountability rules
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lottery/RCT designs; administrative follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Test scores, parent satisfaction, safety, graduation, college enrollment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Voucher effects depend on participating schools and accountability rules; compare offers (ITT) and actual attendance (TOT).
initiatives.oneLineFinding: DC and Louisiana show why voucher evidence cannot be generalized: non-test outcomes may improve in some contexts while test scores can fall in others.

initiatives.name: Magnet schools and controlled choice/desegregation plans
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use themed schools and assignment rules to improve access, integration, and specialized instruction.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Admissions rules, themes, transportation, racial/economic balance targets
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lotteries; court-order changes; quasi studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement, integration, enrollment, graduation, parent demand
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Goals include integration and access, not only test scores; applicant lotteries are not full-population effects.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Magnet effects depend on theme quality, selection, transportation, and whether integration is treated as an outcome or mechanism.

initiatives.name: Community schools / NYC Community Schools
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Integrated academics, health, counseling, family engagement, and community partnerships reduce barriers to learning.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: On-site services, community school director, partnerships, family engagement, attendance supports
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi-experimental impact study; implementation study
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Attendance, chronic absenteeism, credits, achievement, graduation, school climate
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Services, uptake, and neighborhood context vary; compare similar schools and track service dose.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Evidence is promising for attendance and some academic outcomes, but the model is complex and slower-moving than a single curriculum change.

initiatives.name: Harlem Children's Zone / Promise Neighborhoods
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Combine high-quality schools with cradle-to-career supports to change neighborhood trajectories.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Charter schools, parenting programs, health/social services, afterschool, college supports
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi-experimental; school lottery; neighborhood comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement, college, family services, neighborhood indicators
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Separate school effects from neighborhood services; treatment exposure varies by age and service take-up.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The strongest measured gains often come from the school component, while broader place-based effects are harder to isolate.

initiatives.name: Social and emotional learning programs
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Teach self-management, relationship, and decision-making skills to improve behavior, climate, and academics.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: SEL lessons, teacher routines, schoolwide norms, adult SEL, climate strategies
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Meta-analyses; RCTs; implementation studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: SEL skills, behavior, mental health, achievement, climate
initiatives.normalizationIssues: SEL outcomes rely on validated scales and can be politically redefined; implementation quality matters.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Meta-analytic evidence supports positive average effects, though program content and measurement vary widely.

initiatives.name: PBIS / MTSS behavior systems
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Improve behavior by explicitly teaching expectations and using tiered supports and data systems.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Behavior expectations, reinforcement systems, office discipline referrals, tiered intervention teams
initiatives.targetPopulation: Whole schools; students needing behavior support
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Group RCTs; implementation studies; research database
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Office referrals, suspensions, climate, achievement, fidelity
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Discipline data are partly reporting artifacts; fidelity tools are needed to distinguish adoption from use.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Good evidence for behavior/climate improvements; academic effects are often indirect through instructional time.

initiatives.name: Restorative practices
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Replace exclusionary discipline with relationship repair and community accountability.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Circles, restorative conferences, staff training, coaching, discipline policy changes
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Cluster RCT; quasi studies; implementation evaluation
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Suspensions, climate surveys, achievement, safety incidents
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Suspension outcomes change when reporting and discipline policy change; academic effects may vary by grade level.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Can reduce suspensions and improve climate, but academic effects are not automatically positive and depend on execution.

initiatives.name: Attendance and chronic absenteeism interventions
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Improve learning by increasing presence and engagement through information, nudges, case management, and supports.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Parent messaging, attendance teams, transportation, case management, early warning systems
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs of messaging; quasi district studies; early warning validation
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Attendance, chronic absenteeism, course passing, achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Define chronic absenteeism consistently; compare pre-pandemic and post-pandemic baselines carefully.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Attendance is a crucial mediator after COVID, but interventions vary from low-cost nudges to intensive case management.

initiatives.name: Head Start
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Provide preschool, health, nutrition, and family services to improve school readiness for low-income children.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Preschool access, comprehensive services, family engagement, health screenings
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: National randomized Head Start Impact Study; follow-ups
initiatives.outputsMeasured: School readiness, cognition, parent practices, later school outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Control children may access other care; fadeout on tests does not rule out later non-test effects.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The national RCT found early positive impacts with substantial fadeout on many early academic measures.

initiatives.name: Perry Preschool / Abecedarian-style intensive early childhood
initiatives.theoryOfAction: High-quality early education plus family engagement can produce long-run human capital and social benefits.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Low ratios, highly trained teachers, home visits, intensive early learning, health/nutrition supports
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Randomized experiments; long-term administrative/survey follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Education, earnings, health, crime, welfare, intergenerational outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Historic small samples and unusually intensive models may not generalize to scaled public pre-K.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Classic studies show large long-run benefits, but they are not evidence that every scaled pre-K program will replicate them.

initiatives.name: Tennessee Voluntary Pre-K
initiatives.theoryOfAction: State-funded pre-K should improve readiness for low-income 4-year-olds and later school success.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Pre-K access, curriculum, classroom quality, teacher credentials, state oversight
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Longitudinal RCT in oversubscribed sites; RDD component
initiatives.outputsMeasured: School readiness, achievement, special education, discipline, retention, high school outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: RCT estimates apply to oversubscribed programs; quality and counterfactual care differ from other states.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A cautionary scaled pre-K case: short-run gains did not translate into broad long-run academic benefits in the evaluation.

initiatives.name: Boston universal pre-K
initiatives.theoryOfAction: High-quality public pre-K can improve long-run attainment and behavior even when test effects fade.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Public pre-K access, teacher quality, curriculum, centralized enrollment, classroom quality
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Admissions lottery; long-term administrative follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: SAT-taking, college enrollment, graduation, discipline, state test scores
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Lottery applicants and Boston implementation may not generalize; long-term non-test outcomes are essential.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Shows that test-score fadeout can coexist with meaningful long-run gains in college and discipline outcomes.

initiatives.name: Full-day kindergarten
initiatives.theoryOfAction: More early instructional time improves readiness and early academic skills.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Length of kindergarten day, curriculum, teacher staffing, childcare replacement
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi studies; district/state comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Early literacy/math, attendance, later achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Need distinguish added instructional time from childcare and from selection into full-day programs.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Often improves short-run early skills, but durability varies with subsequent instruction quality.

initiatives.name: Summer learning programs
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Add structured academic and enrichment time during summer to reduce summer learning loss.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Program days, hours, attendance, teacher quality, curriculum, enrichment, transportation
initiatives.targetPopulation: Elementary and middle school students, often low-income
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; implementation studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Math/reading scores, attendance, SEL/enrichment participation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Attendance is pivotal; researchers compare invitation, enrollment, and high-attendance treatment-on-treated effects.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Benefits are clearest for students who attend enough days and receive well-planned instruction.

initiatives.name: Extended learning time / longer day or year
initiatives.theoryOfAction: More time can increase active learning, enrichment, tutoring, and teacher collaboration.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Minutes/day, days/year, block scheduling, teacher planning time, enrichment
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Causal synthesis; quasi studies; RCTs in specific models
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement, attendance, enrichment, teacher collaboration
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Normalize by active learning time, not scheduled time; additional time can be low-value if poorly used.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Additional time has generally positive but context-sensitive effects, often small to moderate depending on dosage and use.

initiatives.name: Four-day school week
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Condense schedules for cost savings, teacher recruitment, or community preference, sometimes without reducing learning.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: School days/week, daily minutes, total annual hours, attendance, teacher recruitment
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Difference-in-differences; state comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement, attendance, teacher retention, finances
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Total instructional hours and district selection are central; not designed primarily as learning intervention.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Evidence is mixed and often negative when total learning time drops, making it a cautionary time-policy case.

initiatives.name: One-to-one devices / laptop initiatives
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Universal device access enables digital writing, research, collaboration, personalization, and equity of access.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Devices, broadband, LMS, teacher training, digital content, home access
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Meta-analysis; quasi studies; implementation research
initiatives.outputsMeasured: ELA/writing/math/science scores, digital literacy, usage logs
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Separate access from active academic use; device effects depend on teacher practice and content quality.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Meta-analytic evidence shows some positive average effects, but technology access alone is not an instructional model.

initiatives.name: Adaptive and personalized learning platforms
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Algorithms and dashboards tailor practice and feedback to each student's level.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Adaptive software minutes, mastery thresholds, item banks, teacher dashboard use, grouping
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs; matched comparison; usage-log studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Test scores, platform mastery, minutes, completion
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Usage minutes are endogenous; compare teacher-mediated integration and curricular alignment.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Effects range from positive to null; platforms work best as part of coherent instruction rather than stand-alone screen time.

initiatives.name: Generative AI tutoring and AI-school pilots
initiatives.theoryOfAction: AI tutors or teacher copilots may provide scalable feedback, practice, differentiation, and planning support.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: AI chat/tutoring, guardrails, teacher oversight, prompt design, feedback loops, usage logs
initiatives.targetPopulation: Students and teachers in pilot schools
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Pilot studies; early RCTs mostly outside K-12; systematic reviews
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Usage, engagement, homework, formative performance, teacher time, safety incidents
initiatives.normalizationIssues: K-12 causal evidence is early; compare AI-mediated practice to human tutoring and to no-support screen time.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Treat AI as an emerging tool, not a proven replacement for teacher-led instruction or high-dosage tutoring.

initiatives.name: Career Academies
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Small learning communities that integrate academics, career themes, and employer links improve transitions to adulthood.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Career theme, academic/technical integration, employer partnerships, work-based learning, cohorts
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Random assignment longitudinal evaluation
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Earnings, employment, postsecondary, credits, graduation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Random assignment applies to schools able to implement core features; adult labor outcomes matter more than test scores alone.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: One of the strongest CTE-related causal studies, with notable long-run earnings effects especially for young men.

initiatives.name: Modern CTE pathways and concentrator programs
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Structured career pathways improve relevance, credentials, completion, and employment without sacrificing academics.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Course sequences, industry credentials, work-based learning, dual credit, employer partnerships
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Systematic reviews; quasi studies; administrative data
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Graduation, credentials, attendance, college readiness, employment, earnings
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Selection into CTE is a major issue; normalize by pathway quality, sequence completion, and labor-market alignment.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Evidence is increasingly positive for completion and college/career readiness, but quality varies by pathway.

initiatives.name: Early College High Schools
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Combine high school and college coursework so students earn credits and build college-going identity earlier.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Dual enrollment, small school design, college partnership, supports, accelerated credits
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Randomized/lms lottery evaluation; long-term follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: College enrollment, credits, degree attainment, high school graduation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Lottery/randomized access estimates are strong; compare credit quality and transferability.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: One of the strongest causal postsecondary-readiness models, with positive impacts on college enrollment and degree attainment.

initiatives.name: Dual enrollment / AP and advanced coursework expansion
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Earlier access to college-level coursework raises expectations and reduces college credit/time barriers.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Course access, eligibility rules, tuition support, instructor qualifications, credit transfer, exams
initiatives.targetPopulation: High school juniors/seniors and advanced students
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi studies; administrative evaluations; descriptive trend
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Credits earned, exam scores, college enrollment, persistence, degree completion
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Selection is large; researchers use eligibility cutoffs, school fixed effects, and prior achievement controls.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Advanced access can help, but expansion must track pass rates, credit quality, and whether support keeps up with access.

initiatives.name: Algebra for All / college-preparatory curriculum for all
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Ending remedial tracks and requiring college-prep coursework increases rigor and access.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Required Algebra I, elimination of remedial tracks, course placement rules, curriculum requirements
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Interrupted time series; cohort comparisons
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Course taking, grades, failures, test scores, college outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Access metrics can improve while learning falls if supports are insufficient; compare course standards and failure rates.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: The Chicago case reduced course-taking inequities but increased failures and did not clearly improve achievement or college outcomes.

initiatives.name: AVID and college-readiness support models
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Teach academic habits, tutoring, relational support, and college knowledge to students near the academic middle.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Elective course, tutoring, note-taking, college visits, teacher teams, cohort support
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi/descriptive studies; implementation reports
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Course taking, GPA, graduation, college enrollment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Selection into AVID and school implementation are hard to separate from program effects.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Widely used and plausible, but causal evidence is less clean than for early college lotteries.

initiatives.name: School finance reforms / adequacy and equity funding
initiatives.theoryOfAction: More and better-targeted resources can improve school quality, student achievement, and long-run outcomes.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Per-pupil spending, funding formula weights, capital and operating funds, staffing, salaries, class size
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Court-mandated reform event studies; difference-in-differences; administrative cohorts
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Achievement, graduation, adult earnings, poverty, school resources
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Use inflation-adjusted per-pupil spending, exposure years, district fixed effects, and pre-trend checks.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Modern causal finance research rejects the simple 'money does not matter' claim: sustained targeted dollars can matter.

initiatives.name: ESSER and pandemic recovery initiatives
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Federal relief dollars should support recovery through tutoring, summer learning, staffing, mental health, technology, and HVAC/safety.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Relief spending per pupil, tutoring, summer/enrichment, staffing, HVAC, mental health, edtech
initiatives.targetPopulation: Districts and states after COVID disruptions
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: District recovery scorecards; NAEP/state trends; spending/outcome analysis
initiatives.outputsMeasured: NAEP, state tests, achievement recovery, absenteeism, spending categories
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Spending categories are broad; local recovery depends on closure length, absenteeism, staffing, and baseline losses.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Relief funding appears to have aided recovery in many places, but which components drove gains varies by district.

initiatives.name: Remote learning and virtual schooling during COVID
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Maintain continuity when in-person schooling is disrupted or provide flexible virtual options.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Remote modality, synchronous time, devices, broadband, LMS, teacher adaptation, family supervision
initiatives.targetPopulation: K-12 students during school closures or virtual programs
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Natural experiments; state/district closure comparisons; descriptive data
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Learning loss/recovery, attendance, engagement, course completion
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Remote schooling was not one intervention; closure length, home conditions, and prior district capacity are confounded.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Emergency remote learning was generally associated with large losses, especially when it replaced in-person schooling for long periods.

initiatives.name: Family engagement and parent information interventions
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Parents can support learning and attendance when schools provide timely, usable information and partnership structures.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Text messages, report cards, family conferences, home visits, parent training, two-way communication
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs of messaging/info; quasi family engagement studies
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Attendance, homework, course passing, test scores, parent behavior
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Low-cost nudges and intensive home visiting are different treatments; language/cultural fit matters.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Information interventions can be cost-effective, but family engagement is not a substitute for strong instruction.

initiatives.name: Competency-based / mastery-based learning
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Students should progress after demonstrating mastery rather than after fixed seat time.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Mastery thresholds, reassessment, flexible pacing, standards-based grading, credit rules
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Implementation studies; quasi evaluations; emerging evidence
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Course completion, grades, test scores, student agency, graduation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Grades and credits change meaning under mastery systems; researchers need common external outcomes.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Philosophically important but evidence remains heterogeneous and tied to local implementation.

initiatives.name: Project-based learning and inquiry-oriented reform
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Authentic problems and student inquiry build deeper understanding, transfer, collaboration, and motivation.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Projects, inquiry cycles, group work, performance tasks, teacher facilitation, interdisciplinary units
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: RCTs in specific curricula; implementation studies; WWC reviews
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Content tests, performance tasks, engagement, collaboration
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Effects depend on scaffolding and assessment alignment; 'PBL' labels range from rigorous to superficial.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: PBL is strongest when content-rich, well-scaffolded, and assessed on more than generic engagement.

initiatives.name: Chicago double-dose algebra
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Give ninth graders below a prior-score threshold an additional daily algebra support course alongside regular algebra.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Daily mathematics instructional time, algebra support course, course assignment threshold, classroom peer grouping
initiatives.targetPopulation: Chicago Public Schools ninth graders below the policy's prior-math-score threshold
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Regression discontinuity; interrupted time series; longitudinal administrative follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Algebra grades and pass rates, test scores, advanced coursework, graduation, college persistence and degree attainment
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The clearest regression-discontinuity estimate applies near the assignment cutoff; extended time and peer sorting changed together in some schools.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A concrete acceleration-with-support policy with unusually rich evidence on both near-term course outcomes and later postsecondary progression.
initiatives.tags: algebra; extended learning time; Chicago; acceleration

initiatives.name: Principal Pipeline Initiative
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Build a coherent district system for leader standards, preparation, selective hiring, evaluation, and on-the-job support.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Principal standards, preparation partnerships, hiring and placement, evaluation, mentoring, leadership support
initiatives.targetPopulation: Schools receiving newly placed principals in participating districts
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Multi-district matched comparison; implementation study; cost analysis
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading and math achievement, principal retention, district implementation, cost per student
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The intervention is a districtwide package; comparison estimates cannot isolate a single leader-development component or fully rule out district selection.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A rare system-level leadership case with sustained achievement, retention, and cost evidence rather than an isolated training evaluation.

initiatives.name: Dual-language immersion programs
initiatives.years: Long-term K-8 programs; statewide and district expansion
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Teach literacy and academic content through English and a partner language over multiple years to build academic achievement and biliteracy.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Language of instruction, instructional time by language, bilingual staffing, curriculum, enrollment and admissions rules
initiatives.targetPopulation: Elementary and middle-grade students in one-way or two-way immersion programs
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Lottery-based evaluations; What Works Clearinghouse review
initiatives.outputsMeasured: English literacy, mathematics, science, bilingualism, biliteracy
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Programs differ by language pair, entry grade, duration, student composition, and whether bilingualism is counted as an outcome.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: Lottery evidence makes dual language a genuine initiative-level case, though results vary by subject and program design.

initiatives.name: Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS)
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Use attendance, behavior, course-performance data, and a school intervention team to identify and support students before they fall off track.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Early-warning data routines, intervention-team meetings, student risk flags, monitoring and referral processes
initiatives.targetPopulation: First- and second-year high school students in participating schools
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Cluster randomized controlled trial across 73 high schools
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Chronic absence, course failure, GPA, suspension, on-track credits, school data practices
initiatives.normalizationIssues: It is a data-and-response system rather than a single service; implementation fidelity and the interventions selected after a flag vary by school.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: EWIMS reduced absence and course-failure risk indicators in year one but did not yet improve credit accumulation, a useful check on simple data-solution claims.
initiatives.tags: early warning; attendance; dropout prevention; data use

initiatives.name: San Francisco ethnic studies curriculum pilot
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Offer a culturally relevant ninth-grade course designed to improve engagement, academic identity, and progress for students at risk of disengagement.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Culturally relevant curriculum, ninth-grade course assignment, instructional content, teacher preparation and implementation
initiatives.targetPopulation: Participating San Francisco ninth graders assigned around an eighth-grade GPA threshold
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Fuzzy regression discontinuity
