initiatives.outputsMeasured: Attendance, GPA, credits earned
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The result identifies effects near one assignment threshold in a particular pilot and does not establish a uniform effect for all culturally relevant coursework.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A large, policy-relevant engagement and credit-accumulation case with strong local causal identification and limited external scope.
initiatives.tags: ethnic studies; cultural relevance; engagement; San Francisco

initiatives.name: Comprehensive teacher induction
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Support novice teachers with full-time mentors, training, professional development, and observation opportunities to improve practice, retention, and student learning.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Full-time mentoring, mentor training, professional development, observation and feedback opportunities
initiatives.targetPopulation: Beginning elementary teachers and their students in districts without preexisting comprehensive induction
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: School-level randomized controlled trial
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Teacher support, classroom practice, teacher retention, reading and mathematics achievement
initiatives.normalizationIssues: One- and two-year offers differ, treatment intensity changed over time, and later positive subset results need separation from the main null results.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A prominent randomized counterexample: more structured induction did not reliably improve retention, practice, or achievement despite changing the support teachers received.
initiatives.tags: teacher induction; mentoring; novice teachers; null results

initiatives.name: Community Eligibility Provision / universal free school meals
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Offer meals to all students in eligible schools without individual applications, reducing stigma and household food costs.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Universal meal access, application requirements, school meal participation, household food budget
initiatives.targetPopulation: Students and households in schools eligible for the Community Eligibility Provision
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Quasi-experimental exposure analysis
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Household food purchases, dietary quality, food insecurity, meal participation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Eligibility is related to local poverty and school composition; the principal evidence is on household resources rather than academic outcomes.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: An important whole-child policy with credible food-security evidence, but not yet an academic-effect claim in this dossier.
initiatives.tags: school meals; food security; universal access; poverty

initiatives.name: National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Program
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Combine a five-month residential phase with academic, life-skills, and service components followed by a year of mentoring to reconnect young people to education and work.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Residential alternative education, academic instruction, life-skills training, physical training, mentoring, transition support
initiatives.targetPopulation: Young people disconnected from conventional high-school pathways who are eligible for the program
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Ten-site random-assignment evaluation with three-year follow-up
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Diploma or GED attainment, college credits, employment, earnings, youth development outcomes
initiatives.normalizationIssues: A selective, intensive residential alternative cannot be compared directly with ordinary school reforms on cost, population, or dosage.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: One of the strongest alternative-pathway evaluations, with positive education, employment, and earnings outcomes for a highly disadvantaged population.
initiatives.tags: alternative education; dropout recovery; employment; residential

initiatives.name: Enhanced Reading Opportunities / Reading Apprenticeship and Xtreme Reading
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Replace an elective with a year-long supplemental literacy course for ninth graders who enter high school substantially below grade level in reading.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: Supplemental literacy class, elective replacement, teacher training, explicit reading-comprehension instruction
initiatives.targetPopulation: Ninth graders reading at least two years below grade level
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Student-level randomized controlled trial across two cohorts
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Reading comprehension, state ELA and math tests, GPA, credits accumulated
initiatives.normalizationIssues: The two program models differ; short-run gains did not persist after the program year and students remained substantially behind grade level.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A large multi-site RCT shows meaningful short-run literacy and course-progress gains, alongside a clear warning about fadeout and remaining need.
initiatives.tags: adolescent literacy; reading apprenticeship; ninth grade; RCT

initiatives.name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Provide safe after-school academic enrichment and youth-development activities in high-poverty schools.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: After-school supervision, enrichment activities, academic support, program attendance, family engagement
initiatives.targetPopulation: Elementary and middle-school students in funded high-poverty school communities
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Elementary random assignment; middle-school matched comparison; national implementation evaluation
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Academic achievement, safety, supervision, behavior, social and emotional development
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Attendance intensity was modest and the federal grant is an umbrella for diverse local program designs.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A large, real federal program whose evaluation found few academic impacts, better perceived safety for elementary participants, and mixed developmental effects.
initiatives.tags: afterschool; federal program; safety; null results

initiatives.name: Talent Development High Schools
initiatives.theoryOfAction: Reorganize large, low-performing high schools into smaller learning communities, including ninth-grade and career academies, with a college-preparatory sequence.
initiatives.inputVariablesChanged: School structure, learning communities, ninth-grade academies, career academies, curriculum sequence, student support
initiatives.targetPopulation: Students in large high schools with low achievement, attendance, and graduation outcomes
initiatives.evaluationDesigns: Matched comparison reviewed by the What Works Clearinghouse
initiatives.outputsMeasured: Progressing in school, staying in school, graduation
initiatives.normalizationIssues: Structural and curriculum changes occur together, evidence is limited, and the reviewed comparison may not represent every academy or turnaround model.
initiatives.oneLineFinding: A real school-restructuring model that belongs in the dossier precisely because the reviewed evidence did not show a discernible progress-in-school effect.
initiatives.tags: small learning communities; dropout prevention; high school restructuring; null results

comparisons.title: Screens harm development vs technology enables learning
comparisons.dek: What adult-guided task, for which learner, replaces what prior activity, and with what measured learning gain?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether digital mediation is inherently developmentally costly or a scalable way to increase practice, feedback, and access.

continuum.explanation: Technology effects depend on what activity the tool replaces and whether adult-guided instructional design is present.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: The evidence is mixed: device access and some laptop programs can help, but technology alone is not an instructional model; K-12 generative AI evidence is still early.
comparisons.betterQuestion: What adult-guided task, for which learner, replaces what prior activity, and with what measured learning gain?
commonMisreadings: active, teacher-mediated technology and AI is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Passive/replacement screen time is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Whole language / balanced literacy vs phonics / Science of Reading
comparisons.dek: How do we guarantee code mastery without narrowing reading to decoding drills?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether reading is learned naturally through rich literacy exposure or requires systematic instruction in the alphabetic code.

continuum.rightPole: explicit code-based instruction plus language comprehension
continuum.explanation: Strongly favors explicit code instruction, while keeping vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and background knowledge in the model.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: The evidence strongly supports explicit foundational skills, but reading comprehension also requires vocabulary, background knowledge, fluency, and text experience.
comparisons.betterQuestion: How do we guarantee code mastery without narrowing reading to decoding drills?
commonMisreadings: explicit code-based instruction plus language comprehension is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Meaning-first immersion and cueing is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Knowledge-rich curriculum vs generic skills
comparisons.dek: What content sequence gives students the background knowledge needed to transfer skills?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether comprehension and reasoning are mostly general skills or depend on accumulated content knowledge.

continuum.rightPole: teach transferable strategies like critical thinking
continuum.explanation: Comprehension and reasoning depend heavily on domain knowledge; generic strategies alone are too thin.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: Knowledge-rich approaches are gaining causal support; generic skills are easier to name than to teach without content.
comparisons.betterQuestion: What content sequence gives students the background knowledge needed to transfer skills?
commonMisreadings: teach transferable strategies like critical thinking is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Build domain knowledge and vocabulary is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Direct instruction vs inquiry/project-based learning
comparisons.dek: For which content, prior knowledge level, and assessment type does inquiry beat explicit teaching?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether teachers should first explain and scaffold or let students construct understanding through inquiry.

continuum.explanation: Novices usually need explicit modeling and practice; inquiry works best when content-rich and scaffolded.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: Novices often need explicit instruction; inquiry and PBL can work when content-rich and heavily scaffolded.
comparisons.betterQuestion: For which content, prior knowledge level, and assessment type does inquiry beat explicit teaching?
commonMisreadings: student exploration and authentic projects is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Explicit modeling and practice is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Standardization/accountability vs professional autonomy
comparisons.dek: Which outcomes should be common and which decisions should remain local?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether coherent external pressure improves equity or narrows learning and undermines professionalism.

continuum.explanation: Transparent standards and measurement help, but high-stakes systems narrow behavior and invite gaming.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: Accountability can focus attention and raise some math outcomes, but high-stakes systems create threshold gaming and curriculum narrowing.
comparisons.betterQuestion: Which outcomes should be common and which decisions should remain local?
commonMisreadings: local discretion and teacher judgment is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Common standards, tests, and consequences is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Choice/markets vs common public system
comparisons.dek: What school model and accountability system is being chosen, not just what governance label?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether family choice and school autonomy create improvement or undermine shared capacity and equity.

continuum.explanation: Effects depend on school quality, accountability rules, admissions, transportation, and outcome definition.

comparisons.whatEvidenceSuggests: Effects are highly heterogeneous: some urban charters are strong, while voucher effects vary sharply by state and participating schools.
comparisons.betterQuestion: What school model and accountability system is being chosen, not just what governance label?
commonMisreadings: neighborhood public schools is not a magic phrase; the mechanism and implementation still matter.
Charters/vouchers/magnets is not automatically wrong in every context; outcomes and students differ.
comparisons.whatWouldChangeOurMind: Comparable causal evidence across settings showing durable gains on achievement, progression, and implementation quality would move this synthesis.

comparisons.title: Central curriculum / HQIM vs teacher-created materials
comparisons.dek: What adaptations preserve the high-leverage content and task quality of the curriculum?
comparisons.philosophicalDisagreement: Whether coherence and quality control outweigh teacher autonomy and adaptation.
